observations: A large rounded form fills most of the canvas against a pale blue-grey ground, with a wide open mouth showing a row of teeth outlined in gold-yellow zigzag stitching across the lower half.
The right side carries a single large spiral eye ringed in dark red and yellow; the left side holds a smaller, squinting eye shape with horizontal striped fill — both sit above the mouth.
Short zigzag and sawtooth lines in yellow, red, pink, blue, and green run along edges and down a column below the mouth, layering over each other in distinct parallel bands.
reading: A pale, close-cropped form pushes to the edges of the frame, leaving little open space. The two eyes are built from entirely different marks — one a tight spiral, one a flat stripe — giving the face an off-balance quality. Gold zigzag stitching traces the mouth like a seam under pressure. The layered sawtooth bands below read as something held together rather than settled.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #252 and nnxyz nnotb #254. Where #252 places a similar face against deep black with dense surrounding marks, #253 opens the ground to pale grey, making the face feel more exposed.

connections.reason: Both works center a large face with mismatched eyes and a wide toothed mouth ringed in gold-yellow zigzag lines, but #252 surrounds its face with a black field of dense marks while #253 leaves the face open against pale grey.

lookingQuestion: The two eyes are built from completely different mark types — what does that difference do to how you read the face as a whole?
ambiguities: The red triangular form at upper left could be read as an ear, a horn, or an unrelated shape; the image does not resolve this.

nnxyz #35 shares a toothed grin motif but belongs to a different collection family and its crowded multi-figure composition offers no strong formal parallel beyond that single element, so it was omitted.
